## Summary

Add a reusable **resource HUD component** to `@ui` that renders a game-declared resource set — one labelled item per declared key, in declaration order, with the current value, the declared maximum where the key is bounded, and a **printed** marker for the loss-bearing / irreversible subset — so a five-key story-line economy is legible in play without bespoke per-game scene text.

The engine seams that feed it already ship: `StorylineResourceProjection` exposes `resources`, `irreversible` and `getResources`, and bounds are validated manifest data. Only the presenter is missing.

## Problem statement

A game can now *declare* and *enforce* an arbitrary resource set — keys, per-key bounds and a never-restored subset — but the UI layer has no component that renders that declaration. `src/ui/index.ts` exports card, hand and pile views plus a single-line `HintBar`, and the one five-key in-repo economy (`GymLongErasureScene`) hand-rolls its status line with `resourcesLine()` / `resourceLabel()`.

So the GDD's five-key economy (`hull`, `morale`, `stores`, `goodwill`, `charge`) cannot be presented consistently: every game that declares a set re-implements label casing, declaration order, bound display and a loss-bearing marker, and nothing stops a game from marking `hull` by colour alone — which the presentation contract (§3.4.3) forbids.

## Users

- **Game / scene developer** — builds a declared-economy HUD in a few lines from the projection and the manifest instead of a bespoke text line.
  - *As a game developer, I want to pass a declared key set, a resource bag and the manifest's bounds to one component and get a legible HUD, so I do not re-implement label casing, ordering and marker logic per game.*
- **Content designer** — the declared maximum and the loss-bearing subset are visible, so the bounds authored in §2.8.2 read as part of the interface rather than as hidden data.
  - *As a designer, I want a key's cap and its "losses only" nature shown in the HUD, so a full hold or an irreversible key reads correctly to the player.*
- **Player** — can see all five keys, their current values and caps, and which key is a one-way loss.
  - *As a player, I want to name what each key protects and see when a key is full or loss-bearing, so the economy's trade is legible without a help panel.*
- **Accessibility reviewer** — the loss-bearing and bound-state cues carry a printed channel, so the HUD is not colour-dependent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A reusable resource-HUD component (exported from the `@ui` barrel, `src/ui/index.ts`) renders a caller-declared resource set: exactly one labelled item per declared key, in declaration order, each showing the key's display label and current value, with no resource key, label, order or value hard-coded in the component.
- A bounded key renders its declared maximum alongside the current value (for example `Morale 5 / 8`); a key at its declared maximum and a key at its declared minimum are each distinguishable by a **printed** channel as well as any colour cue.
- A key in the declared irreversible / loss-bearing subset is marked by a **printed** channel (the word `irreversible`, or an equivalent glyph with accompanying text) beside the key as well as by colour, matching the "Irreversible key" row of GDD §3.4.3.
- A value update (`setResources(bag)` or equivalent): under reduced motion (the caller-resolved `getEffectiveReducedMotion()` flag) snaps to the new value with no tween and plays **no** SFX; otherwise it animates the change and plays at most one `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` SFX per update through the injected `SoundManager`, and is a silent no-op when no `SoundManager` is supplied.
- `GymLongErasureScene` renders its `statusBar.resources` surface through the new component (declared keys, display labels, irreversible set and bounds from the committed `long-erasure-episode.json`; values from the resource projection's `getResources`) instead of the bespoke `resourcesLine` / `resourceLabel`, and keeps its existing observable behaviour (starting resources, per-choice resource changes, layout anchor) green in the browser suite.
- Unit tests for the component (headless, mocked Phaser) cover: label / order / value rendering from a resource bag; bound display and the at-maximum and at-minimum printed markers; the irreversible printed + colour marker; a value change that spilled or clamped; the reduced-motion instant, silent path; exactly one SFX on an animated update; and idempotent `destroy()`.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents the component (Shared HUD Components), `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` and the scene help text are updated if the rendered chrome changes, and `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §2.8.6 item 7, §3.1's Engine status column and §6's G8 row move from "filed / no component" to "delivered" naming the component and its plain-data contract.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players can see every resource key the economy declares — with its cap and its loss-bearing status — in one consistent HUD row, so a five-key trade is legible in play instead of being a bare comma-separated text line.

## Constraints

- **Plain data in, plain data out.** `src/ui` does not import `@story-line` today and must not start: the component takes a resource bag (from `projection.getResources(state)`), the declared keys, and optional `bounds` / `irreversible` / `labels` records — the same "plain options object" shape as `TokenPileView` and `HintBar`.
- **Bounds are supplied by the caller.** The projection does not expose its `bounds` option, and the engine hard-codes no key or range; the caller passes the manifest's `readManifestBounds` output (as the Long Erasure scene already does for content loading).
- **Position comes from SLL.** The caller passes the point resolved by `anchorPoint()` (plus relative offsets inside the anchor), never a literal coordinate. The component supports left / centre / right alignment around that anchor point, because the Gym's `statusBar.resources` anchor is right-aligned (`setOrigin(1, 0.5)`).
- **Phaser-bearing module.** The component lives in `src/ui/`, is exported from the `@ui` barrel, and is **not** added to `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` — the `check:ui-node-surface` prebuild gate must keep passing.
- **Colour is never the only channel** (GDD §3.4.3). The printed marker is the primary cue; contrast targets WCAG AA (4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text / UI boundaries).
- **Reduced motion is honoured from the resolved flag** (GDD §3.4.1): no tween and no SFX under reduced motion; the textual channel is never suppressed.
- **No presentation guessing.** A key with no supplied label prints as authored (`hull` → `hull`, capitalised at most) — the `formatOptionCost` precedent of not inventing plural rules for an arbitrary key.
- **Optional audio.** `SoundManager` is injected and optional; a missing manager is a silent no-op, never a crash, and SFX keys come from `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` (no game-scoped string literals).
- **Read-only HUD.** No resource mutation, no click-to-spend, no game-logic side effects; an optional update hook exists only for observability/tests.
- **No engine-seam changes.** Bounds (G4) and irreversibility (G5) are already delivered; this item adds the presenter only.

## Existing state

- `src/ui/index.ts` — exports `HandView`, `PileView`, `TokenPileView`, `HintBar`, panels and overlays, but no component that renders a declared resource bag.
- `src/ui/TokenPileView.ts` — nearest precedent: token stack with live count labels, SLL-positioned by the caller, click handling, `tests/ui/tokenPileView.test.ts`.
- `src/ui/HintBar.ts` — compact single-`Text` status strip, `tests/ui/HintBar.test.ts` (mocked-Phaser headless pattern).
- `src/ui/UIComponentBase.ts` — shared lifecycle (`destroyed`, `enabled`, `destroy()` idempotence, tracked listeners).
- `src/ui/ReducedMotion.ts` — `getEffectiveReducedMotion()` (explicit flag → Settings toggle → `prefers-reduced-motion`).
- `src/ui/Renderer/index.ts` — `createHudText()` helper used by the Gym scene for HUD text.
- `src/story-line/resources.ts` — `StorylineResourceProjection` exposes `resources`, `irreversible`, `getResources(state)` and the bounded `applyResourceDelta`; `createResourceProjection(fields, { bounds, irreversible, onRemainder })` accepts bounds but the projection does not expose them.
- `src/story-line/content/episode-manifest.ts` — `resources.declared`, `resources.irreversible`, `resources.bounds` are validated manifest data; `readManifestBounds` reads bounds fail-closed.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymLongErasureScene.ts` — builds `statusBar.resources` as one `createHudText` with origin `(1, 0.5)`; renders `this.resourcesLine(this.run.resources)`; helpers `resourcesLine()` and `resourceLabel()`; scene exposes `getRunState()`, `getAvailableOptionLabels()`, `getFeedbackText()`, `getJournalLines()`, `getPlayedSfxKeys()`.
- `example-games/gym/layouts/gym-long-erasure.layout.json` — `statusBar` zone with `act`, `clock` and `resources` anchors (no `nextBeatCost` / `losses` anchors at this commit).
- `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure-episode.json` — declares `hull, morale, stores, goodwill, charge`; `irreversible: ["hull"]`; bounds `hull 0–5`, `morale 0–8`, `stores 0–6`, `goodwill 0–5`, `charge 0–4`.
- `tests/ui/HintBar.test.ts`, `tests/ui/tokenPileView.test.ts` — headless mocked-Phaser test conventions for `@ui` components.
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureScene.browser.test.ts` — browser suite asserting the scene's start state, resource changes and layout binding.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — "Shared HUD Components" and "Hand & Pile Rendering" sections; `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` — the Long Erasure scene row.

## Desired change

1. **New component module** (indicative: `src/ui/ResourceHud.ts`, exported from `src/ui/index.ts` with its option types), built on `UIComponentBase`.
2. **Indicative options:** `{ x, y, align?, resources, declaredKeys, bounds?, irreversible?, labels?, reducedMotion?, soundManager?, sfx?, onChange?, style? }`; a `setResources(bag)` update method; an idempotent `destroy()`.
3. **Render:** one item per declared key in declaration order — label, current value, and `value / max` where bounded; printed state markers for at-maximum, at-minimum and irreversible (plus the secondary colour cue).
4. **Update:** an animated value change (short tween/pop) with at most one `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` SFX; instant and silent under reduced motion; no animation of layout beyond the value change.
5. **Gym adoption:** replace `resourcesText` / `resourcesLine` / `resourceLabel` in `GymLongErasureScene` with the component at the same SLL anchor, fed from `LongErasureContent`'s declared keys, the manifest's `irreversible` and `bounds`, and the run's resource bag.
6. **Docs:** developer reference, Gym index/help text and the GDD's delivered-status rows, per the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/ResourceHud.ts` — new component: rendering, update path, reduced-motion branch, SFX, destroy.
- `src/ui/index.ts` — barrel export and exported option types.
- `tests/ui/resourceHud.test.ts` — new headless unit suite (arbitrary key sets, bounds, irreversible marker, reduced motion, SFX once, destroy).
- `tests/ui/resourceHud.browser.test.ts` — optional rendered-probe test if the text/marker assertions need a real renderer.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymLongErasureScene.ts` — adopt the component at `statusBar.resources`; remove the bespoke line helpers.
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureScene.browser.test.ts` — keep/extend the observable HUD assertions after adoption.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Shared HUD Components entry.
- `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` — Long Erasure scene row.
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — §2.8.6 item 7, §3.1 Engine status, §6 G8 row.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: over-fitting to the five GDD keys.** Mitigation: plain-data API plus unit tests over an arbitrary key set (`supply`, `heat`, …).
- **Risk: declaration-order / label drift.** Mitigation: render order is exactly `declaredKeys`; labels are caller-supplied and fall back to the key as authored; tested.
- **Risk: colour-only signalling regression.** Mitigation: printed markers are part of the ACs and asserted in tests.
- **Risk: the reduced-motion path being an untested afterthought.** Mitigation: explicit AC + tests for instant, silent updates.
- **Risk: SFX spam / audio in headless runs.** Mitigation: at most one SFX per update, animated path only, absent manager is a no-op.
- **Risk: breaking the Gym browser suite.** Mitigation: keep the scene's observable helpers and assertions; change only how the same values are rendered.
- **Risk: scope creep into adjacent presentation.** The live loss-ledger line, the epilogue ledger, the act/scene banner (G9), affordability labels and the objective panel stay out of scope; anything that grows becomes a linked work item.
- **Assumption:** the component is read-only; the optional `onChange`-style hook is an observability/test seam, not gameplay.
- **Assumption:** adopting the component in `GymLongErasureScene` is in scope — it is the in-repo five-key economy and the G8 definition is "without bespoke scene text"; this also matches the G4/G7 precedent of migrating the Gym consumer.
- **Assumption:** the component name may be `ResourceHud` (the item title) or `ResourceBar` if it renders more naturally as a bar; the barrel export and docs pin whichever ships.
- **Assumption:** no engine (`@story-line`) change is needed; bounds are already validated data and the projection exposes the declared set and irreversible subset.

## Out of scope

- The live loss-ledger line (`statusBar.losses`) and the epilogue ledger — game-side text per GDD §3.1 / §3.2.
- Act/scene transition presentation (G9, `CG-0MWR0BJBU005TDTT`).
- Surfaced-affordability presentation on options (G7 delivered) and the objective panel.
- `EconomyLedger` generalisation, condition expressiveness (G6), and the bounds / irreversible engine seams (G4 / G5 — delivered).
- Keyboard/pointer interaction for the read-only HUD (none required by §3.4.4).

## Related work

- `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` — GDD engine-gap backlog (source item; complete); entry G8 of `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.
- `CG-0MWNFVLYT003M7XF` — GDD epic (complete); identified the resource-HUD gap.
- `CG-0MWPY2CHF003AHE1` — GDD presentation contract (complete): `statusBar.resources` zone/anchors, colour-independent signalling, reduced-motion and SFX rules.
- `CG-0MWR0BGVG004UE7X` — **G4** bounds/spill/clamp (done): the bounds the HUD displays and the spill/clamp the display can reflect.
- `CG-0MWR0BHH9002OQUZ` — **G5** irreversible policy (done): the loss-bearing subset the HUD marks.
- `CG-0MWR0BI3S008K9Y6` — **G7** surfaced affordability (completed): adjacent presentation; the option shortfall text is its own surface.
- `CG-0MWR0BG9H007AFNU` — **G3** scene-space guard (sibling gap).
- `CG-0MWR0BJBU005TDTT` — **G9** act/scene banner (sibling presentation gap; disjoint surface).
- `CG-0MWSJYLZ3005C2V1` — **G2** manifest `resources.start` / `resources.bounds` data (done).
- `CG-0MWQZJEXQ002G3KE` / `CG-0MWQZHFA0006AOVX` — the declared-resource seam in adapters.
- `CG-0MWNHZ67Q005BWE0` — declared resource set in the story-line engine (`createResourceProjection`, `DEFAULT_RESOURCE_KEYS`).
- Precedents: `src/ui/TokenPileView.ts` (token stack with count labels), `src/ui/HintBar.ts` (status strip), `src/ui/UIComponentBase.ts` (lifecycle).

## Plan

Decomposed into five vertical slices (test-first inside each slice). Dependency order:

1. `CG-0MWZ9W5SF0094QHM` — **ResourceHud: render a declared resource set** (AC1; component + barrel export + headless render tests).
2. `CG-0MWZ9W8VG008LUZS` — **ResourceHud bounds and irreversible printed markers** (AC2, AC3; depends on 1).
3. `CG-0MWZ9W9F5001ZPF2` — **ResourceHud value updates, reduced motion and SFX** (AC4, AC6; depends on 1, 2).
4. `CG-0MWZ9WDWS004NJ8Y` — **Adopt ResourceHud in Gym Long Erasure** (AC5; depends on 2, 3).
5. `CG-0MWZ9WD9P003IAQM` — **Document ResourceHud and flip GDD G8 status** (AC7, AC8, AC9; depends on 4).

**Test-first note.** Each slice authors its headless tests before the implementation and makes them green inside the same child. A standalone "write red tests" child is deliberately not created: the repository gate requires `build → test → commit` on a green tree, so a child that only adds failing tests could not pass its own push gate. The Gym browser suite is extended only where the rendered text/markers need direct observation.

**Reused / existing seams.** `UIComponentBase` lifecycle, `createHudText()` (`src/ui/Renderer/index.ts`), the `TokenPileView` / `HintBar` options-object precedent, `createResourceProjection(...).getResources` and caller-supplied `readManifestBounds(...)` output, `getEffectiveReducedMotion()`, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, and the existing `statusBar.resources` SLL anchor.

**Vertical-slice check.** Every feature cuts through code, headless tests, and the documentation its ACs name; the final slice carries the cross-cutting docs/GDD flip and the full-suite gate. Between slices, the next child's description is reviewed and updated if the preceding slice changed an interface.

**Out of scope (unchanged from intake).** Live loss-ledger line, epilogue ledger, G9 act/scene banner, affordability visuals, objective panel, and any `@story-line` change.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-27 — Decomposed `CG-0MWR0BIPV0074WLM` into 5 child features in dependency order (2, 3, 4, 5 depend on earlier slices); AC coverage review reports 100% (`proceed`); effort/risk unchanged (Medium / Low).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Should the component take a `StorylineResourceProjection` or plain data?**
  - **Answer (agent, research):** plain data — `resources` (bag), `declaredKeys`, optional `bounds` / `irreversible` / `labels`. A search of `src/ui/` found no `@story-line` import, so `@ui` stays engine-agnostic; `StorylineResourceProjection` already exposes `getResources` and `irreversible`, but not `bounds` (bounds live in `ResourceProjectionOptions`), so the caller supplies them. Source: `src/ui/**` grep, `src/story-line/resources.ts` (`StorylineResourceProjection`, `ResourceProjectionOptions`).
- **Q2 — Should the Gym Long Erasure scene adopt the component in this item?**
  - **Answer (agent, research):** yes. G8's definition is a rendered view "without bespoke scene text"; the scene currently hand-rolls `resourcesLine()` / `resourceLabel()` at `statusBar.resources`, and the sibling gaps adopted their seams in the Gym (G4 migrated the resource projection; G7 wired `isOptionAffordable`). Source: `example-games/gym/scenes/GymLongErasureScene.ts`, `wl show CG-0MWR0BGVG004UE7X`, `wl show CG-0MWR0BI3S008K9Y6`.
- **Q3 — Component name and alignment support?**
  - **Answer (agent, routine):** `ResourceHud` from the item title (the implementer may ship `ResourceBar` if it reads more naturally; docs and the barrel pin the shipped name). Alignment is needed because the Gym anchor is right-aligned (`setOrigin(1, 0.5)`); the component takes the SLL anchor point plus an alignment option rather than assuming left-aligned text. Source: `GymLongErasureScene.buildChrome()`, `example-games/gym/layouts/gym-long-erasure.layout.json`.
- **Q4 — Is the live loss-ledger line (`statusBar.losses`) part of this component?**
  - **Answer (agent, research):** no. G8's stated scope is the resource set, its maximum and its loss-bearing marker; §3.1 treats `statusBar.losses` as a separate line, and §3.2 makes the epilogue ledger the permanent record. Keeping it out avoids inventing ledger formatting in the engine. Source: `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §3.1, §3.2, §6 G8.
- **Q5 — Should the HUD show at-maximum / at-minimum state?**
  - **Answer (agent, research):** yes — the item's proposed unit tests name "spill/clamp display", and G8 requires the maximum. It is rendered as value + declared maximum plus a printed state marker (colour is secondary), per §3.4.3. Source: work-item description ("Unit tests: … spill/clamp display"); `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §3.4.3, §6 G8.
- **Q6 — SFX under reduced motion?**
  - **Answer (agent, research):** none. §3.4.1 states that with reduced motion enabled "SFX are suppressed"; the animated path plays at most one `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` SFX, the reduced-motion path plays none. Source: `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §3.4.1.
- **Q7 — Are bounds available on the projection for the HUD to read?**
  - **Answer (agent, research):** no; `createResourceProjection` consumes `bounds` for clamp/spill arithmetic but the `StorylineResourceProjection` interface exposes only `resources`, `irreversible`, `getResources` and `applyResourceDelta`. The caller passes `readManifestBounds(...)` output, exactly as the Gym scene already does for content loading. Source: `src/story-line/resources.ts`, `example-games/gym/scenes/GymLongErasureScene.ts`.

- **Q8 — Should the plan create a standalone red-test child to satisfy test-first ordering?**
  - **Answer (agent, repo policy):** no. Each slice authors its tests first and makes them green before committing; the repository gate requires a clean build and a passing changed-scope test gate before any commit (AGENTS.md, "Never commit without … build → test → commit"), so a child that only adds failing tests could not pass its own gate. Test-first is therefore enforced *inside* each slice, and the per-slice ACs name the tests they ship.
- **Q9 — Does "Full project test suite must pass" mean the final slice runs the full suite?**
  - **Answer (agent, repo policy):** yes, the AC is carried as written; the final child runs `/skill:test` (full), records the green result and the dev-push gate re-enforces it. The typed `unit` profile remains the minimum during the earlier slices.
- **Q10 — Is a separate browser test for the component required?**
  - **Answer (agent, research):** not by default. The ACs require headless unit tests, and the adopted Gym browser suite exercises the rendered HUD. A rendered probe is added only if a text/marker assertion cannot be observed headlessly. Source: `tests/ui/HintBar.test.ts` (headless precedent); parent Key Files lists `tests/ui/resourceHud.browser.test.ts` as optional.
- **Q11 — What printed wording marks at-maximum and at-minimum?**
  - **Answer (agent, assumption):** `full` and `empty` printed beside the always-present `value / max`; the implementer may refine the words in review, but the printed channel is mandatory (GDD §3.4.3). The GDD pins only the `irreversible` wording, so this is a documented reasonable assumption rather than a producer decision.

No genuine producer decisions were required; every open point was answerable from the repo, the GDD or sibling work items, so no producer-review hold was raised.

# Engine gap: keyboard choice navigation and overlay focus order

## Problem statement

The story-line presentation contract promises a full keyboard path — choose an
option with `1`–`6` or arrows + Enter, traverse focus inside an open overlay and
activate with Enter/Space, and close only the topmost modal with Escape — but the
engine exports no helper for any of it, so every game must hand-roll `keydown`
listeners. Today only the panels' own toggle keys are bound, which makes
[GDD §3.4.4](docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md#344-keyboard-and-touch-input-paths)
aspirational and leaves §3.8 unable to claim the keyboard path is testable.

## Users

- **Keyboard-only / switch-access player** — plays the whole story-line run without
  a pointer: `1`–`6` (or arrows + Enter) picks a choice, Tab/Shift+Tab walks an
  open overlay's controls, Enter/Space activates, Escape dismisses only the
  modal on top.
  - *As a keyboard-only player, I can select a choice with a digit key so I never
    have to locate option rows with a mouse.*
  - *As a keyboard-only player, I can reach and activate every control in an open
    journal/confirmation overlay with Tab and Enter, and Escape closes only that
    overlay.*
- **Game developer (story-line build epic, Gym maintainer)** — attaches two shared
  helpers and inherits the keyboard contract plus its tests instead of
  re-implementing listeners per scene.
  - *As a developer, I call `attachChoiceNavigation(scene, …)` once per scene and
    get digits, arrow wrap, Enter/Space activation and a disposer, so the keyboard
    path cannot drift between games.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/ui` exports two additive helpers from the `@ui` barrel — `attachChoiceNavigation(scene, { count, onChoose, onHighlight?, keys? })` and `attachOverlayFocus(scene, focusables, { onEscape, onFocusChange? })` — each returning an idempotent disposer, with no change to existing `Overlay`/`OverlayManager`/`OverlayButton` signatures required by callers.
- Choice navigation maps in-range digit keys (`1`–`9`) to option indices, moves the highlight with ArrowUp/ArrowDown plus ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (wrapping at both ends), activates the highlighted option with Enter/Space via `onChoose(index)`, reports the highlighted index through `onHighlight(index)`, and is completely inert while a managed overlay is open or after disposal.
- Overlay focus traverses the supplied focusables in list order (Tab forward, Shift+Tab backward, wrapping), activates the focused item with Enter/Space via that item's `onActivate`, reports focus changes through `onFocusChange(index)` so the game can render a visible focus state, and closes only the topmost managed overlay on Escape — never a lower modal, never the game, and it leaves Escape unhandled when no managed overlay is open (so `SettingsPanel`'s default `Escape` toggle keeps working, per GDD §3.2 rule 3).
- Both helpers install and remove their `keydown`/scene-`shutdown` listeners through an injectable keyboard seam so they are unit-testable headless (same seam pattern as `src/ui/narration-reveal.ts`), never throw when the scene has no keyboard plugin, and leave no listener behind after disposal or scene shutdown.
- Headless unit tests cover digit selection (including out-of-range), arrow wrap in both directions, Enter/Space activation, focus traversal and wrap, Escape closing the topmost overlay only, inertness while a modal is open, and disposer/shutdown teardown; one browser test proves the real `scene.input.keyboard` wiring and the rendered focus state on a parented overlay.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (the new helper section and, if the module qualifies, the node-safe surface manifest), and the GDD status rows that currently read "Gap B7" (§3.4.4, §3.6 B7, §3.8 and §6 G11), plus the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Impact

A keyboard-only player can play a story-line run end to end — pick choices by
number or arrow, walk an overlay's controls, and dismiss only the modal on top —
instead of being forced back to the pointer.

## Constraints

- **Small effort band** (0.5–2 days, GDD G11): one new `src/ui` module plus tests
  and doc flips. No new dependency, no refactor of the overlay primitives.
- **Headless-testable by construction.** Keyboard access must go through an
  injected seam (`{ on, off }`-shaped) rather than a direct `scene.input` reach,
  matching `narration-reveal.ts`'s `bindInput` pattern; the module should stay
  Phaser-type-only so it can join the node-safe `src/ui` manifest.
- **No key-binding collisions.** `HelpPanel` (`?`) and `SettingsPanel` (Escape)
  keep their own listeners; the new Escape handler must be stack-aware, not a
  second global listener that fights them (GDD §3.2 rule 3).
- **No bespoke overlay work.** Focusables are game-owned objects parented into
  `hudContainer`; the helper wires keys and reports focus, it does not build
  overlays. `OverlayDialogHandle.close()` remains the close path.
- **Accessibility floor preserved.** A visible focus indication is mandatory: the
  helper must make the focused item visually distinct (via `onFocusChange` plus a
  default style hook), and there must be no motion dependency (reduced motion is a
  no-op because nothing animates).
- **Out of scope (record as linked follow-ups, not scope creep):** screen-reader
  live-region announcements, DOM (`tabindex`) focus management for DOM-rendered
  debug tools, arrow-key navigation of the market/card rows, and a Gym demo scene
  (the GDD requires the helper, not a new Gym scene).

## Risks and mitigations

- **Key-stealing risk** — a global `keydown` listener that swallows digits or
  Enter could break a scene's own bindings. *Mitigation:* the helpers consume
  only the keys they own, expose `isBlocked()`, and are inert without a
  registered focus/choice context; a test pins "no binding when disposed".
- **Escape double-handling risk** — `SettingsPanel` already defaults to Escape.
  *Mitigation:* stack-aware handling plus the "unhandled when no managed overlay
  is open" test (GDD §3.2 rule 3).
- **Accessibility theatre risk** — navigation that works but has no visible focus
  is unusable. *Mitigation:* mandatory `onFocusChange`/`setFocusVisual` contract
  and a browser test that asserts the rendered focus state.
- **Listener-leak risk** — early returns on scene shutdown can leave listeners.
  *Mitigation:* one disposer path used by the disposer, the `shutdown` hook and
  the error path; a test asserts every `on` has a matching `off`.
- **Scope-creep risk** — screen-reader live regions, DOM `tabindex` focus for
  debug tools, market/card arrow navigation and a Gym demo are attractive but
  out of scope; they are recorded as linked follow-ups rather than folded in.
- **Assumption:** the GDD's wording ("`1`–`6`, or arrows + Enter") is the whole
  contract; any additional keybinding scheme requires a producer decision before
  implementation.

## Existing state

- `src/ui/index.ts` exports the overlay primitives (`createOverlayBackground`,
  `createOverlayDialog`, `dismissOverlay`, `OverlayManager`,
  `ParameterizedOverlay`) but no keyboard helper.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` registers its own `keydown` listener in
  `setupKeyboardShortcut()` and removes it in `destroy()`; `SettingsPanel.ts`
  does the same for `Escape`/end-turn capture; `SettingsStore.ts` exposes
  `getEndTurnKeybind()`/`setEndTurnKeybind('Enter')` for one game action only.
- `src/ui/OverlayManager.ts` already enforces one live overlay (`showOverlay()`
  dismisses the previous one) but tracks objects, not a modal stack, and binds no
  keys. `src/ui/Overlay.ts` exposes `OverlayDialogHandle.close()`.
- `src/ui/ParameterizedOverlay.ts` and `src/ui/OverlayButton.ts` are
  pointer-only (`pointerover`/`pointerout`/`pointerdown`), so their buttons are
  currently unreachable by keyboard.
- `src/ui/narration-reveal.ts` is the established headless pattern: it binds
  `scene.input.keyboard` defensively through `bindInput(...)` and skips a
  destructor-less input object.
- Precedent for a keyboard picker exists only as a **game-local DOM overlay**
  (`../tce-main-street/src/debug/MarketCardCheatOverlay.ts`, arrows + Enter +
  Escape on a DOM input); it is not reusable from the engine and does not cover
  Phaser overlay objects.
- Nothing in `src/ui` reads `'Tab'`, `'Enter'` or digit keys today (verified by
  grep), so the new bindings introduce no regression to existing scenes.

## Desired change

Add one additive keyboard module (working name `src/ui/keyboard-navigation.ts`)
with a pure, injectable core:

```ts
export interface KeyboardSeam {
  on(event: 'keydown', handler: (event: KeyboardEvent) => void): void;
  off(event: 'keydown', handler: (event: KeyboardEvent) => void): void;
}

export interface ChoiceNavigationOptions {
  count: number;                       // visible options
  onChoose(index: number): void;       // Enter/Space or digit activation
  onHighlight?(index: number): void;   // arrows / digits moved the highlight
  keys?: { digits?: boolean; arrows?: boolean; activate?: boolean };
  keyboard?: KeyboardSeam;             // defaults to scene.input.keyboard
  isBlocked?(): boolean;               // e.g. true while a modal is open
}

export interface OverlayFocusable {
  onActivate(): void;
  setFocusVisual?(focused: boolean): void;  // game-owned visual
}

export interface OverlayFocusOptions {
  onEscape(): void;                    // pop the topmost managed overlay
  onFocusChange?(index: number): void;
  keyboard?: KeyboardSeam;
}

export function attachChoiceNavigation(
  scene: Phaser.Scene | null | undefined,
  options: ChoiceNavigationOptions,
): () => void;

export function attachOverlayFocus(
  scene: Phaser.Scene | null | undefined,
  focusables: OverlayFocusable[],
  options: OverlayFocusOptions,
): () => void;
```

Semantics: digit keys select (and activate, or highlight+activate — decided in
plan against the GDD wording) indices `0..count-1`; arrows move the highlight
with wrap; Enter/Space activates; Tab/Shift+Tab walk the overlay focus list with
wrap; Escape pops only the topmost managed overlay. Helpers no-op safely with a
null/headless scene, are inert while blocked, and dispose every listener on the
returned disposer and on scene `shutdown`.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/keyboard-navigation.ts` — new module: seam types, pure index/traversal
  reducers, `attachChoiceNavigation`, `attachOverlayFocus`, disposer plumbing.
- `src/ui/index.ts` — barrel exports for the two helpers and their option types.
- `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` — add the module if the surface check proves it
  Phaser-value-free (Phaser is type-only).
- `src/ui/OverlayManager.ts` — optional additive managed-modal stack (or the new
  module owns its own stack; the plan picks one, with no caller breakage).
- `tests/ui/keyboard-navigation.test.ts` — new headless unit suite (injected seam).
- `tests/ui/keyboard-navigation.browser.test.ts` — new browser suite proving real
  `scene.input.keyboard` wiring and the focus visual on a parented overlay.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — helper reference section (hotkeys, focus order, Escape
  stack, reduced-motion no-op, headless seam).
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — §3.4.4 status rows, §3.6 B7, §3.8
  "keyboard path is untestable", §6 G11 disposition.

## Related work

- `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` — GDD engine-gap backlog (source of G11).
- `CG-0MWR0BAT30015DPQ` — the build epic that consumes this capability.
- `CG-0MWR0BJBU005TDTT` — sibling engine gap G9 (act/scene transition
  presentation); same presentation-contract family.
- `CG-0MWR0BL4Q000OYG6` — sibling engine gap G12 (shared verbosity preference).
- `CG-0MWPY2CHF003AHE1` — GDD presentation contract (UI, audio, accessibility)
  that defines §3.4.4 and the B7 gap.
- `CG-0MTINKHUT009KHK5` / `CG-0MTIR0HK4005SEQW` — completed Market Card Cheat
  tool: game-local keyboard picker precedent (arrows + Enter + Escape), not a
  shared helper.
- `CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN` — node-safe `@ui` surface manifest and check (constrains
  how the new module must be importable).

### Duplicate-check outcome

Performed (`wl search` over "keyboard focus overlay", "accessibility", "choice
list"). No completed item satisfies this item's ACs: the only keyboard-navigation
work is the Market Card Cheat/Tool pair, which is a **game-local dev tool**
DOM overlay, not a shared `@ui` helper, and does not cover focus order or
topmost-only Escape. Partial-overlap note recorded in
[Related work](#related-work).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

All questions below were resolved from repository evidence or a documented
reasonable assumption (the shared interview contract's **routine** class); none
required a producer decision, so the item was not held for producer review.

- **Q: Is the scope exactly GDD G11 (choice navigation + overlay focus), or does
  B7 also require keyboard activation of narrative/journal page controls?**
  — Answer (routine, documented assumption): page controls are implemented as
  focusable overlay items, so `attachOverlayFocus` makes them Tab-reachable and
  Enter/Space-activatable with no extra API. Evidence:
  [GDD §3.4.4](docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md#344-keyboard-and-touch-input-paths)
  lists paging under the same B7 row and §3.2 requires journal page buttons as
  the non-wheel path. No separate paging helper is in scope.
- **Q: Which keys move the highlight — arrows only, or also `1`–`6`?**
  — Answer (routine, documented assumption): both, per the GDD (`1`–`6`, or
  arrows + Enter). Digits are out-of-range safe (indices beyond `count` are
  ignored) and arrows wrap.
- **Q: Does Escape in the new helper collide with `SettingsPanel`'s default
  Escape toggle?** — Answer (routine, documented assumption): no, because the
  helper only consumes Escape when a managed overlay is open and GDD §3.2 rule 3
  already forbids opening an engine panel and a managed modal simultaneously; a
  test will pin "Escape with no managed overlay is unhandled".
- **Q: Should the helpers render a focus highlight themselves?** — Answer
  (routine, documented assumption): no artwork ships; the helper reports
  `onFocusChange(index)` and calls an optional `setFocusVisual(focused)` so the
  game keeps ownership of its option rows. A visible focus state is still an AC,
  proven by the browser test.
- **Q: Does this need a Gym scene?** — Answer (routine, documented assumption):
  no. The GDD requires the engine capability (and its tests), and G11's effort
  band is `S`; a Gym demo would push it to `M` and is recorded as out of scope.
- **Q: Does the module belong in the node-safe `@ui` manifest?** — Answer

  `npm run check:ui-node-surface` passes with Phaser as a type-only import;

- **Q: Issue type and priority?** — Answer (routine): `task` / `low`, as filed

# Shared verbosity preference (Full / Concise)

## Problem statement

The story-line game's GDD defines a Full/Concise verbosity setting (§3.4.2) that should persist across games and sessions, but the engine currently has no shared verbosity preference: `SettingsStore` persists tooltips, reduced motion, the end-turn keybind, card design and the event-log palette, yet verbosity exists only as a game-local `SettingsPanel.extraToggles` entry with no storage key. Reading-comfort preferences should follow the player, not the game, exactly as tooltips and reduced motion already do.

## Users

- **Players of narration-bearing games** (e.g. the planned story-line game): want their Full/Concise reading preference to survive across sessions and to carry over to other games that support verbosity.
- **Game developers** (engine consumers): want a one-call `getVerbosity()` / `setVerbosity()` API plus a first-class panel toggle, rather than re-implementing a storage-backed preference per game.

Example user stories:

- As a player, I want my "Concise" choice to persist so I don't re-select it every session — like my tooltips and reduced-motion preferences already do.
- As a developer, I want a shared engine API so my narration-heavy game gets persistence and a settings-panel control without writing a bespoke storage key.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` exposes typed `getVerbosity()` / `setVerbosity()` for the `'full' | 'concise'` union, backed by a storage key (proposed `tce-verbosity`), mirroring the `getTooltips()` / `setTooltips()` shape (storage parameter with `null` to disable access; safe fallback when storage is unavailable; invalid stored values fall back to the default).
- Default when unset, or when storage is unavailable / corrupt, is `'full'` (the GDD §3.4.2 default); a stored `'concise'` round-trips through `setVerbosity` → `getVerbosity`.
- `SettingsPanel` renders the verbosity preference as a first-class control in the Display section (two-option selector "Full" / "Concise", following the existing Card Design text-option pattern), gated by a `hasVerbosity` config flag so games without narration never show a no-op control; the panel reads the stored value on build/open and persists changes via `setVerbosity`.
- Unit tests extend `tests/ui/SettingsStore.test.ts` for the storage seam: default when unset, non-default round-trip, unavailable/unusable storage (both `null` backend and thrown access), and invalid stored value resolving to the default; a browser test in the style of `tests/ui/SettingsPanelTooltips.browser.test.ts` proves the panel control renders only when `hasVerbosity` is set, reflects the persisted value on open, and persists a change.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (at minimum `docs/DEVELOPER.md` Settings Panel section and the AGENTS.md §13 HUD key-APIs reference; update the GDD §3.4.2 status cell / §6 G12 disposition to mark the gap as delivered).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players of narration-heavy games can set a Full/Concise reading preference once and have it persist across sessions and games, instead of re-toggling it per game.

## Constraints

- **Small scope (estimate `S`, ~6.8 h incl. overheads):** one storage key, one getter/setter pair, one panel control, plus tests and docs — nothing more. No event-emitter wiring, no per-game migration, no changes to existing consumers' behaviour.
- Precedence: mirror the tooltips preference pair in `SettingsStore.ts` and the existing panel toggle wiring; do not redesign the settings panel layout.
- Non-boolean two-valued choice: the API is an enum string `'full' | 'concise'`, not a boolean; any invalid stored string resolves to the default (`'full'`).
- **Scope boundary:** the engine only stores, exposes and renders the preference. What `Concise` suppresses (auxiliary feedback line, inline journal ticker — never authored prose) is game-owned behaviour, implemented by the consuming game, not by this item.
- Existing preferences and `extraToggles` callers are unaffected — the new control is additive.
- Doc-update policy applies (engine-facing API change), so `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` change in the same commit.

## Existing state

- `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` persists `tce-selected-difficulty`, `tce-endturn-keybind`, `tce-show-tooltips`, `tce-card-design`, `tce-ui-event-log-palette`; reduced motion lives in `src/ui/ReducedMotion.ts` (`tce-ui-reduced-motion`). There is no verbosity key or getter/setter (`getTooltips`/`setTooltips` at lines ~197–224 are the shape precedent; `getCardDesign`/`setCardDesign` at ~73–104 show a validated string-valued preference).
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` renders engine-owned toggles (Tooltips when `hasTooltips`, Reduced Motion) plus a game-local `extraToggles` list; Card Design renders as a row of selectable text options (`handleCardDesignSelect` at ~1474) — the control precedent for a two-option verbosity selector.
- GDD §3.4.2 table row: *Verbosity | Full / Concise | Full | game-owned key via a SettingsPanel `extraToggles` entry | **Partly available** — the toggle seam exists; shared persistence is gap B8*. The B8/G12 rows say shared persistence is the missing piece; this item delivers it.

## Desired change

- Add `VERBOSITY_DEFAULT = 'full'`, storage key `tce-verbosity`, and `getVerbosity()` / `setVerbosity(value)` in `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` (consumers import it as `@ui/SettingsStore`, matching `getTooltips` — the `src/ui/index.ts` barrel does not re-export settings helpers).
- Add a first-class Display-section control in `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` behind a `hasVerbosity?: boolean` config flag (default `false` — opt-in, so a game with no narration shows no no-op control). The control presents "Full" and "Concise" as selectable options and persists via `setVerbosity`.
- Wire `hasVerbosity` through `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel`. Note the existing positional parameter list already has seven entries, so append `hasVerbosity` as the last optional parameter (after `extraToggles`) to avoid churning existing call sites.
- Tests + docs as per ACs.

## Key Files:

- `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` — Add `VERBOSITY_DEFAULT`, `tce-verbosity` key, `getVerbosity()` / `setVerbosity()` (imported by consumers via `@ui/SettingsStore`; no barrel change).
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — `hasVerbosity` config flag, new Display-section control (Full/Concise), persistence on change.
- `src/ui/CardGameScene.ts` — Forward `hasVerbosity` through `initSettingsPanel` (mirror `hasTooltips`).
- `tests/ui/SettingsStore.test.ts` — Extend with verbosity coverage (default, round-trip, unavailable storage, invalid value).
- `tests/ui/SettingsPanelVerbosity.browser.test.ts` — New browser test in the `SettingsPanelTooltips.browser.test.ts` style: flag gating, stored value reflected on open, change persisted.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Settings Panel control list + new-control paragraph.
- `AGENTS.md` — §13 HUD key-APIs reference (`getVerbosity()`/`setVerbosity()` from SettingsStore).
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — §3.4.2 status cell + §6 G12/B8 disposition updated to "delivered" (small text changes only).

## Related work

- `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` — Source backlog: the GDD engine-gap backlog this item was filed from (entry G12).
- `CG-0MWNFVLYT003M7XF` — Parent epic: GDD (completed); §3.4.2 defines the verbosity setting.
- `CG-0MWR0BAT30015DPQ` — Gap-delivery epic (completed): delivered the other GDD engine gaps; this orphaned item predates it.
- `CG-0MWR0BKIT0084ZID` — Companion engine gap: keyboard choice navigation and overlay focus order (open, task, low).
- `CG-0MRO5W3CL000CNGO` — Precedent: "Card style preference is not persisted" (completed) — demonstrates the storage-backed preference pattern for a visual comfort setting.
- `CG-0MP2A64K8007B7EE` — Precedent: Standard HUD components: help, settings, overlays, status bar (completed).
- Duplicate-work detection performed via `wl search "verbosity"` and `wl search "tooltips preference"` — no overlapping completed or open item covers a shared verbosity preference; the only match is this item itself.

**Related work (automated find-related report, `find-related` skill):**

- Related work items: `CG-0MLUH07HP1QKGS1Y` — Settings Panel with mute toggle and volume slider (completed; origin of the panel's toggle pattern), `CG-0MLSGNPFI0ZX35FR` — Directory Structure and Placeholder Modules (completed), `CG-0MM3B31S50OYMC59` — Define Setup Types in Core Engine (completed).
- Repository matches: `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` (defines the requirement — §3.4.2, §6 B8/G12), `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (Settings Panel reference — must be updated), `AGENTS.md` (§13 HUD key-APIs — must be updated).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (recorded):** default when unset is `'full'` — taken directly from GDD §3.4.2 ("Full (default)"); no producer decision needed.
- **Assumption (recorded):** invalid stored values (unknown string, garbage) resolve to `'full'` rather than being preserved — mirrors `getCardDesign`'s stored-key validation.
- **Assumption (recorded):** the control is opt-in via `hasVerbosity` (default `false`), because a game without narration/scoring prose has nothing for the setting to affect; games that support verbosity pass `true`. This mirrors the `hasTooltips` opt-out but inverted (opt-in) since most current games have no narration. If the producer prefers the control always visible, that is a one-line default change.
- **Assumption (recorded):** the control is a two-option "Full"/"Concise" selector rather than a boolean ON/OFF toggle, so the visible meaning matches the enum values (Card Design text-option precedent). A plain toggle would be semantically ambiguous.
- **Assumption (recorded):** no live change event is needed — like tooltips/reduced motion, consumers read `getVerbosity()` when rendering; the story-line game (not yet built) is the first consumer.
- **Scope-creep risk:** demonstrating the toggle in a Gym scene (e.g. `GymTooltipScene`) would make the change visible but grows the item beyond the `S` band; it is deferred and can be filed as a follow-up when the first narration-bearing game consumes the API.
- **Risk:** the `hasVerbosity` flag adds a config surface; keep it minimal and documented to avoid bloating `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel`'s already-wide (seven-parameter) list — append it last and update the JSDoc.
- **Risk (regression):** `SettingsPanel`'s Display section is laid out with hard-coded `y` offsets; a new row must reuse the existing offset chain (`cardDesignY`, `endTurnY`, …) so panels with every control enabled still fit and remain scrollable.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Does the shared verbosity preference already exist anywhere in the engine?" — Answer (repo search, verified): No. `SettingsStore.ts` has no verbosity key; only `extraToggles` (game-local) exists. Source: `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` (keys at lines 3–8), GDD §6 B8/G12.
- Q: "What is the default value when no preference is stored?" — Answer (GDD §3.4.2): `Full` is the documented default. Source: `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §3.4.2 table row "Verbosity | Full / Concise | Full".
- Q: "Should the control be always visible or gated?" — Answer (documented assumption, Intake): gated behind a new `hasVerbosity` config flag, default `false` (opt-in), mirroring `hasTooltips` so narration-free games show no no-op control.
- Q: "Should the engine emit an event when verbosity changes (live re-render)?" — Answer (documented assumption, Intake): No — precedent is that tooltips/reduced motion are read via getters at render time; no event mechanism exists for them, so none is added here.
- Q: "Can a boolean toggle represent Full/Concise, or should the control show both labels?" — Answer (documented assumption, Intake): a two-option "Full"/"Concise" selector, following the Card Design text-option precedent, so the rendered labels match the enum values.

No open questions remain.
